newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Eritrean acquitted of bid to kill Mengistu.
newsitem.headline: Eritrean acquitted of bid to kill Mengistu.

text.p: A Zimbabwean court on Friday acquitted an Eritrean accused of conspiring to kill exiled Ethiopian strongman Mengistu Haile Mariam but jailed him for five years for illegal possession of firearms.

High Court Judge Paddington Garwe said he had agonised over sentencing Solomon Haile Gabre Michael because the accused had suffered severely under Mengistu's rule and had also been mistreated by Zimbabwean police after his arrest last November.
Illegal possession of firearms carries a maximum life imprisonment term in the southern African country.
"I have agonised over the question of sentence. I have asked myself what purpose is to be achieved by incarcerating the accused who has obviously lost so much in his life," Garwe said.
"It's clear that the accused's conduct, though clearly unlawful, was the result of experiences he underwent at the hands of the ruling junta or Dergue as it came to be known," Garwe said.

During the trial, Solomon, who pleaded not guilty to all charges, told the court his private parts were permanently damaged due to torture he said he endured when he was imprisoned in 1979 for opposing Mengistu's Marxist regime.
"The exhibits produced show serious violations of the rights of civilians, the wanton killing of civilians," Garwe said of news video tapes and newspaper cuttings the defence showed to the court.
"It's public knowledge that there are court proceedings currently taking place in Ethiopia in which members of the junta have been cited by defendants," the judge said.

In the Ethiopian capital of Addis Ababa, 46 of the former officials of the Dergue are in the dock. Twenty-five others, including Mengistu, are on trial in absentia for genocide and crimes against humanity during their 1974-1991 rule.

On Friday, Justice Garwe said of Solomon: "The accused's experiences at the hands of the authorities in Ethiopia are a relevant consideration....This is a case where justice should be done but tempered with mercy".

He said he had also taken into account the defence's evidence that Solomon had lost the use of his right arm after he was shot by Zimbabwean police close to where Mengistu was taking a stroll in the Harare suburb where he has lived since when he fled in 1991.
He said local police had delayed seeking treatment for his wound and had also stolen more than U.S.$4,000 from him.
He granted an application by the defence to appeal against the sentence.
